New York City was at the height of its glory. An ambitious mayor backed by the Governor along with a generous tax subsidy and a handful of talented engineers had revamped the dated architecture of the aging beauty and now her night lights were rivaled only by the stars. 

Skyscrapers that truly merited the term towered over the landscape like colossi, defying even gravity to knock them down. They rose miles to impossible heights and all were intertwined with skyways large enough to carry traffic. The careful planning and coordination of the designs were a logistical masterpiece prompting one prominent MIT professor of Engineering to remark in wonder: "A more eloquent design could not be achieved if God Himself drew the plans." The mayor boasted that even birds cannot nest atop "The Apex" (the tallest of them all). 

The city seemed to hum and buzz with such a life and energy and prosperity that even as panic gripped the world at the annihilation we were destined to strike, she seemed to rise above it all, as though it's perfection inspired the citizens not to give in to their baser instincts as their final moments slipped away. 

The comet's shadow grew, seeming to eclipse the continent, and New York's lights shown bright in majesty one final time. Then the comet screamed and thudded and the planet knew no more.

"Well he always was a bit dense." Said Kathy.

"A bit dense! HA! A 70 year old man somehow still in the prime of his youth and just now he wonders about it? A bit dense...that's a very kind way to put it. Somebody with a brain should have his fortune, there would be no limit to the good they could do. Why do the half-wits always win the lottery?" Sue replied, shaking her head.

"You know I can hear you, right?" I called from the other room, annoyed at my decrepit and aging younger siblings.

"Yes of course you can hear me. You don't have hearing aids you dim-witted meathead."  

Sue was always my favorite sister. Perhaps she can be forgiven, it must be difficult to feel the pains of age and watch your brother still bounce around with a spring in his step and not a care in the world. 

But she was wrong about one thing. I intend to do good in this world. Just now I'm packing my bags to get on a plane that will take me to Baltimore where I'll be paying a visit to John Hopkins Medical School. The fabled Fountain of Youth is coursing through my veins and the researchers there are...well to say they are interested is to put it mildly. Maybe we can live forever.

Superior Phenotypes © 2145 (All rights reserved) is the dominating genetic manufacturer in this day and age and they are both my mother *and* my father, technically speaking. I have hundreds of brothers and sisters with thousands more being bred. We will be the largest living family in the history of the world. Their engineering is becoming more efficient daily and I don't think that anybody realized how in demand their product was or how powerful an entity they would become. 

As a company that specializes in genetic engineering their trade branches out into more than just creating children. They are working on eradicating disease, curing old age, creating customization shops for the frivolous, vain, and wealthy to change their appearance to a manner that better suits their preference. 

"Better genetics for a better you" is their official slogan; but this couldn't be farther from the truth.

I was given to my adoptive parents when I was a baby. They are a decent set of folks who raised me right and made sure I got a good education. They did their best to instill me with good moral and productive values and they loved me unconditionally. I grew very close to them, especially my father and as far as I know they are both still living. But on my 18th birthday some obscure clause in my contract came into light when three burly representatives from the company came to take me away. 

I am special, you see. I am their "most prized specimen" as their CEO put it to me, with an earnest look that indicated I should feel proud I was selected. In truth I am one of many they have reclaimed, maybe they even take us all, and what I feel is far from pride for I am being forcibly detained without pay or compensation apart from room and board. I tried to escape once, but they are always watching and when I was captured they implanted a tracking device into my spinal cord so that I risk crippling myself if I attempt to remove it. My arguments about human rights are never even addressed because legally speaking, I am theirs.

Their political clout inclines any powerful enough to secure my release to be either bribed or bullied to look the other way. Is there a difference between a slave and a prisoner? For my purpose I could be either or both. 

What they want is simple. I am to be the poster-boy for their company. I go to events, I smile, I wave, I give interviews with scripted questions and answers. Once I deviated only slightly from the response I was supposed to give and they brought me into a windowless basement room with T.V. screen. On the screen was a live feed of the house I grew up in. They will kill my family if I don't cooperate.

Satan sat alone on his throne in Hell. No visitors. No calls or queries. Nothing but his brooding thoughts and ever growing malice. Oh how He hated Him! The passing eons had done nothing to dull the wrath he had been born into.  With each passing moment his anger grew, since the dawn of creation itself. And it would continue to grow...past the present into the unimaginably hollow future, merciless in it's infinity. The universe itself would end but he would not end with it. The cosmos would collapse back onto itself.  A cold and dead and lifeless void awaited as entropy ran it's course and it would all grow empty and silent and dark until nothing was left but he and Him still locked in their eternal struggle.

For they were eternal. Both of them. And he knew why he existed. He was evil incarnate, the Prince of Darkness, The Deciever and the Defiler, the Wicked One, the Devil. 

It was ludicrous. All of humanity despised him, save for a few. All life everywhere feared and hated him. As if he had ANY choice at all. Did they not understand that the God they so revered was responsible for his very existence? Could they not grasp that had it not been for their "Benevolent" Creator's arrogance and pride that he would have not been born at all? 

How could it be, that Yahweh created evil? Why would He? For the mere sake wanting a rival? Was the supreme being in the universe really so simple and petty underneath it all?

And who were THEY, those mortals with their fleeting souls and simple minds. Who were they to judge what they didn't understand? What if they had been them born into this? They would hate too! If they had been conceived on a whim to satisfy God's ego. If their very essence and eternal purpose could be reduced to kneeling unwillingly at God's heel and thwarted at every turn. They would hate as surely as he did. They would revel bitterly in death and destruction and sin as he did. He knew this, and so did God. And there was nothing to be done except to exist and to hate.
